**DATASCI 406 FA 26, Quiz 1.3**

**Name and Uniqname:**

## Question 1 (1 point)

To estimate the bias of $\hat\theta$ you simulate $k$ datasets of size $n$ and
run `t.test(theta_hats - theta)`. You rerun with a much larger $k$, leaving $n$
unchanged. What gets smaller? **Circle one.**

1. $\Var{\hat\theta}$ --- the estimator itself becomes more precise.
1. The `t.test` interval around the estimated bias --- we pin the bias down better.
1. $\text{Bias}(\hat\theta)$ --- the estimator itself becomes less biased.
1. All three: a longer run improves every number the simulation reports.

## Question 2 (1 point)

You simulate to check whether `t.test(x)$conf.int` really covers 95% of the
time for skewed data. Which ingredient does the simulation need that a real
data analysis can never supply? **Circle one.**

1. The true value of $\theta$, so we can check whether the interval caught it.
1. A sample size $n$ matching the dataset we actually have.
1. Enough replications $k$ that the reported coverage is precise.
1. A confidence level $1 - \alpha$ fixed before looking at the data.

## Question 3 (3 points)

$X_1, \ldots, X_{10}$ are i.i.d. $N(\mu, \sigma^2)$ with $\sigma^2 = 1$. Two
estimators of $\sigma^2$, run on the same $k = 100{,}000$ simulated datasets:

$$S^2 = \frac{1}{n - 1} \sum_{i=1}^n \left(X_i - \bar X\right)^2
\qquad\qquad
\hat\sigma^2_{\text{MLE}} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \left(X_i - \bar X\right)^2$$

| | bias | variance |
|---|---|---|
| $S^2$ | $0.00$ | $0.22$ |
| MLE | $-0.10$ | $0.18$ |

Circle the estimator you would use and justify it in two or three sentences.
You must say **both** (i) which single quantity ranks the two, and why neither
column settles it alone, and (ii) what that quantity is for each estimator.

Circle: $\;\;\mathbf{S^2}\;\;$ or $\;\;\mathbf{MLE}$
